Key.Original: Manufacturer: Mauser%1Length: 49.2 inches%1Ammunition: 7.92×57mm Mauser%1Rate of Fire: 35 rpm%1Weight: 4.09kg%1Firing Mode(s): Bolt-Action%1Magazine: 5-round stripper clips%1Effective Range: 500 meters%1%1The Gewehr 98 (also known as the G98, Gew 98 or M98) is a bolt-action rifle manufactured by Mauser and adopted by the German Empire in 1898. Chambered in 7.92×57mm Mauser with a 5-round internal magazine, the rifle features a straight bolt handle and a full-length wooden stock. While it was Germany’s main rifle during the First World War, it also saw limited use during Second World War where it was often issued to second-line units and reserves.
